title: Fix the price list
prompt: This function should list every price each product has been listed or sold at, but it stops with an error about casting a product id. Find the bug and fix `solve(product_cdc, invoice_lines)`.
rules: A price counts if it is a `list_price` in `product_cdc` or a `unit_price` on a row of `invoice_lines`.
Return `product_id` and `price`, with each pair once. `price` keeps its decimal type.
A missing value counts as a value, so a missing price is listed once like any other.
hints: Look at the order of the columns in `listed` and in `sold`.
`union` lines columns up by position, not by name, so a price lands under `product_id`.
Select `sold` in the same order as `listed`, or keep it and use `unionByName`, which matches the names.
explanation: `union` stacks columns by position. `listed` is `(product_id, price)` but `sold` is `(price, product_id)`, so Spark tries to put prices and ids in the same column and fails when it casts an id to a number. Select `sold` in the same order, `invoice_lines.select("product_id", F.col("unit_price").alias("price"))`, or keep it and write `listed.unionByName(sold)`, which matches by name. Keep `distinct()`, because the same price usually appears on the product feed and on many invoice lines. `unionByName` without the alias fails too, since `unit_price` and `price` are different names.
